_source: docs/v0_physiology_research_candidates.md and docs/v0_physiology_eval_results.md (Wismer & Christie 1987, GLFC Special Publication 87-3, and cited field studies). Every value below traces to a specific candidate/citation in those documents. Values marked "evidence: weak" carry the same caveat noted there and should be read with more caution.
_units: All values in degrees Celsius unless noted. °F given alongside for readability.

WALLEYE.description: general feeding/activity range, with a field-measured preference point of 20.6°C (69°F) from Trout Lake, Wisconsin
WALLEYE.evidence: solid field telemetry + WI-specific field value (Coutant 1977a via GLFC Sp87-3)

WALLEYE.description: feeding becomes less frequent and more selective below this temperature
spawning begins around 40°F, peak activity commonly cited 44-48°F
WALLEYE.evidence: agency/extension-tier for precise window; underlying trigger mechanism well established

YELLOW PERCH.description: field-measured preference, averaging Lake Michigan (20.8°C) and Trout Lake/Silver Lake, WI (20.2°C) values
YELLOW PERCH.evidence: peer-reviewed growth-performance study + WI/LM field values (GLFC Sp87-3)

LARGEMOUTH BASS.description: thermal optimum for growth; note one study found HIGHER feeding rates at 18°C, so warmer is not uniformly better in the primary literature
LARGEMOUTH BASS.evidence: weak / mixed — conflicting findings within the primary literature itself

SMALLMOUTH BASS.description: thermal preference; field-validated in a Lake Michigan harbor telemetry study
SMALLMOUTH BASS.evidence: solid — field telemetry directly in Lake Michigan

SMALLMOUTH BASS.description: spawning occurs in this range, notably cooler than largemouth bass

NORTHERN PIKE.description: growth-optimum range from lab/experimental physiology studies
pike begin avoiding water warmer than this (coolwater-adapted species)
earliest gamefish to spawn in spring, triggered in this range
NORTHERN PIKE.evidence: extension-tier for precise figure; consistent with supporting cold-temperature physiology

MUSKELLUNGE.description: thermal optimum; activity is documented to decline above 25°C (77°F)

BLACK CRAPPIE.evidence: weak — undergraduate research report is the direct evidence source; preferred-temp figure lacks a clear primary citation

BLUEGILL.description: spawning trigger range, with repeat spawning roughly every 30 days while temperature stays above the peak-initiation point
BLUEGILL.evidence: weak — extension/angling-media-tier for the precise numbers, though the underlying mechanism (temperature-triggered spawning) is well-established general fish reproductive physiology

CHINOOK SALMON.description: Lake Michigan field final-temperature-preferendum value (Coutant 1977a via GLFC Sp87-3). Note: this species tracks the thermocline and may be well below the surface even when surface water reads warmer — a surface-temperature-only comparison is a weak proxy for this species specifically
CHINOOK SALMON.evidence: solid field value, but surface-only measurement is a poor proxy for depth-following behavior

COHO SALMON.description: Lake Michigan field final-temperature-preferendum value (GLFC Sp87-3). Same surface-vs-depth caveat as Chinook applies
COHO SALMON.evidence: solid field value, but surface-only measurement is a poor proxy for depth-following behavior

BROWN TROUT.description: annual modal selected temperature ~12°C, upper preferred limit ~16°C, field value 13.8°C from a Lake Michigan thermal-gradient study
BROWN TROUT.evidence: reasonably strong — field study specifically in/near Lake Michigan

LAKE TROUT.description: cold-water preference range; field value 11.8°C from a Point Beach, Lake Michigan study
LAKE TROUT.evidence: field value solid; general range is extension/secondary-tier synthesis

_excluded.WALLEYE_DIEL_LIGHT: Candidate #1 (walleye dusk/dawn low-light feeding activity) is the single best-evidenced physiological mechanism found across V0's research, but requires a light-condition/time-of-day input this MVP does not compute in v1 (it's about immediate feeding activity, not a seasonal temperature window). Deliberately left out of this reference file rather than approximated.
_excluded.BAROMETRIC_PRESSURE: Explicitly excluded per docs/v0_physiology_research_candidates.md candidate #17 — no primary scientific support found; angling folklore.
